newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World airports record 6 pct cargo rise in May.
newsitem.headline: World airports record 6 pct cargo rise in May.

text.p: World air cargo traffic climbed by six per cent in May, led by double-digit growth in the Middle East and Asia-Pacific region, the Airports Council International said on Tuesday.
Passenger traffic, which expanded by a modest 2.4 per cent in North America, rose globally by 4.6 per cent compared with the same month a year ago, according to the Geneva-based body.

"Strong passenger growth in four regions was masked by a slowdown in the growth rate in the Middle East and in North America for the second month running," ACI's statistics manager Maria Hinayon was quoted as saying in a statement.
"Cargo growth was particularly strong in Asia-Pacific and the Middle East," she added.
Cargo traffic rose to nearly 4.39 million tonnes in the 490 airports monitoring by the ACI in 150 countries.

Memphis, base of U.S. express freight carrier Federal Express, was the world's busiest cargo airport, with 178,307 tonnes, up 2.6 per cent, followed by Los Angeles at 157,155 tonnes, a rise of 9.6 per cent against May 1996, ACI said.

The Middle East posted 12.9 per cent growth in cargo, followed by a 11.6 per cent spurt in Asia-Pacific. Europe recorded a 5.6 per cent rise while North America had 3.7 per cent growth. Cargo traffic in Africa fell off by 16.5 per cent.
Global passenger traffic rose to 220.7 million last May.

Latin America and the Caribbean registered healthy rises of 10.6 per cent in passenger growth, followed by Africa and Europe at nearly eight per cent each. Asia-Pacific had 5.2 per cent growth while the Middle East had just 0.1 per cent growth.
Aircraft movements rose by 3.1 per cent to 4.4 million.
